parsed.diagnosis: FDIR consumes the single isolation on first mild friction fault (residual ~0.46-0.49 mNm, severity 0.2) leaving no isolation for later severe friction/derate/leak and forcing degraded 3-wheel control. Without-policy runs are clean, so premature isolation itself induces attitude loss and saturation.
parsed.rationale: Reserve isolation for hard failures. Mild Coulomb friction trips detector at ~0.00046 Nm but stays controllable in 4-wheel pseudo-inverse allocation. Requiring residual >=0.0005 Nm to isolate keeps mild wheels in control, preserves 4-wheel authority against leaks and momentum build-up, and leaves the one isolation free for later severe derate/friction whose residual exceeds 0.0005 Nm.
parsed.why_no_regressions: Only suppresses isolations below 0.0005 Nm, which are shown controllable without policy. Hard faults still isolate as before. No change to SOC, attitude watchdog, or momentum guard.
